message: In the concealed under-deck support frame (C2), the added-mass girder fatigue demand has needed formal non-critical closure, Retrofit Integration Architect and Manager. To check it I used static plus dynamic bending review reusing the static weight check (E11) with the midspan stress increment (E12). I found about 2.5 Megapascals static plus about 0.3 Megapascals dynamic per girder, according to Eurocode 3, 2005. I propose retaining bolted cross-frames carrying two 200 kilogram modules as fatigue-non-critical. My position: ready because stress range is two orders below endurance. In the under-deck vertical Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) at midspan (C1), the first vertical bending mode control without altering deck sightlines has needed final confirmation, Vibration Control Specialist and Manager. To check it I used modal-response review of the side-view mode-shape layout (E3) with the optimal Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) sizing (E4) and the resonant response calculation (E1) against the controlled-response stroke estimate (E6). I found 1.9 Hertz mode with midspan maximum falling from 1.75 metres per second squared to about 0.20 metres per second squared with 8.2 millimetres stroke, according to Den Hartog, 1934 and Human Induced Vibrations of Steel Structures, 2008. I propose holding hidden midspan placement tuned to 1.86 Hertz with 0.086 damping ratio. My position: ready because mode, frequency and acceleration evidence closes comfort and placement.
